subject.title: [Bug] QQ Bot: skill_workshop approval "Allow" button always recorded as rejected

question: Should QQ Bot direct C2C approval callbacks require an explicit configured owner or approver identity, or may every sender admitted by the DM policy approve privileged plugin operations?
rationale: A private conversation proves message scope but not necessarily owner identity when the bot accepts open or wildcard DMs; changing that rule can grant privileged Skill Workshop actions to unintended users.

options.title: Keep explicit authorization
options.body: Retain the current identity gate, reject the unconditional C2C bypass, and improve configuration guidance and unauthorized-click feedback.

options.title: Add narrow C2C approvers
options.body: Define a dedicated explicit approver resolution path for QQ plugin approvals while keeping ordinary DM admission separate.

options.title: Trust all C2C senders
options.body: Accept the bypass only as an intentional documented security-policy change with live authorized and unauthorized callback proof.

recommendation.title: Keep explicit authorization
recommendation.body: Retain the current identity gate, reject the unconditional C2C bypass, and improve configuration guidance and unauthorized-click feedback.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily an approval-authorization boundary, and repository ownership guidance associates Vincent Koc with security.
